data.long_meaning: From the Old German or Celtic elements renan meaning 'counsel, advice' and wald meaning 'rule, power'. The name Renaud may have originally meant 'wise ruler' or 'wise counselor'. The name Renaud carries the meaning “Adviser, wise counselor” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Renaud usually hope their child will grow to embody adviser, wise counselor and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Renaud is primarily of French origin, and it has a rich cultural history in France. It is the name of several notable historical figures such as Renaud de Montauban, a crusader knight from the House of Montauban, and Jean Renaud, a Commander in the French colonial army. In folklore and mythology, Renaud is the name of a character in the French epic poem "Renard, the Cunning Fox", where Renaud is a king bewitched by the cunning fox and eventually transformed into a stag himself. Renowned French author Emile Zola also had a character named Renaud in his famous novel "The Fortune of the Rogues" (1873).
